question.text: As per SEBI ICDR Regulations, 'Social Enterprise' means:

answer.text: Only a Section 8 Company engaged in the 16 eligible activities
Only an NPO with 12AB and 80G registrations
Either a Not-for-Profit Organisation (NPO) or a For-Profit Enterprise (FPE) that meets the eligibility criteria specified in SEBI ICDR Regulations
Any company registered in India and listed on the main board of NSE or BSE

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Ch 1.3, SEBI ICDR defines an SE as either an NPO or an FPE that meets the eligibility criteria under the regulations (primacy of social intent, engagement in at least one of the 16 activities, target underserved population, 67% threshold for FPE). The Trap: Options A and B narrow to a single legal form. Option D confuses main-board listing with SSE SE-status. The SEBI definition is form-agnostic subject to eligibility. Cross-Exam Context: Cross-links to Ch 2 (SSE Introduction), Ch 3 (Registration), Ch 11 (Key Regulations). The definition is a bedrock concept and appears in multiple chapters. Assessor's Pro-Tip: The SIA's first working-paper entry should recite the SEBI definition and tick-box whether the engaged entity is NPO or FPE. This anchors subsequent eligibility tests and prevents scope-creep during fieldwork.
